Title: User successfully requests OTP and receives it in the response header
Preconditions: User has a valid phone number registered in the system
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the phone number as a query parameter using the payload in testData. 2. Observe the response status code and headers.

Test Data: phoneNumber: "+1234567890"
Expected Result: Response status code is 200. The response body contains the message 'OTP Sent to Your Phone Number'. The 'OTP' header contains the generated OTP value.

Title: Request OTP with phone number containing non-numeric characters
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the phoneNumber query parameter set to a value containing non-numeric characters as shown in testData.

Test Data: phoneNumber=+123-456-7890
Expected Result: The system should return an HTTP 400 Bad Request status code with an error message indicating that the phone number format is invalid.

Title: Request OTP with empty phone number
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the phoneNumber query parameter set to an empty string as shown in testData.

Test Data: phoneNumber=
Expected Result: The system should return an HTTP 400 Bad Request status code with an error message indicating that the phone number is required.

Title: Request OTP and verify the OTP header is not exposed in the response when OTP generation fails
Steps:
1. Mock the OTP generation service to throw an exception. 2. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with a valid phoneNumber query parameter as shown in testData. 3. Verify the response does not contain an 'OTP' header.

Test Data: phoneNumber=1234567890
Expected Result: The system should return an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error status code, and the response should not contain an 'OTP' header.

Title: Verify OTP value is not exposed in the response header after OTP request
Preconditions: A valid phone number is available for testing
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the phoneNumber query parameter set to a valid phone number (e.g., +1234567890). 2. Inspect the response headers and body for the OTP value.

Test Data: phoneNumber: "+1234567890"
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and the body 'OTP Sent to Your Phone Number'. The OTP value is NOT included in any response header or body.

Title: Verify OTP value is not logged or exposed in error responses during OTP verification
Preconditions: A valid phone number and an OTP have been requested and generated
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/verify-otp with an incorrect OTP value. 2. Inspect the response body and logs for the OTP value. 3. Repeat with an expired OTP (if applicable).

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "+1234567890", "otp": "000000"}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and the message 'Invalid or expired OTP'. The OTP value is NOT included in the response body or logs.

Title: Verify brute force protection for OTP verification attempts
Preconditions: A valid phone number and the correct OTP are available for testing
Steps:
1. Send 10 consecutive POST requests to /api/auth/verify-otp with incorrect OTP values for the same phone number. 2. On the 11th attempt, send the correct OTP. 3. Observe the response for each attempt.

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "+1234567890", "otp": "000000"} (incorrect OTP for first 10 attempts, correct OTP for 11th attempt)
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) for all incorrect attempts. The correct OTP on the 11th attempt may be rejected or rate-limited (e.g., HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests).
